subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a pulley system, adding more pulleys (more supporting ropes) generally:
options: Reduces the effort needed to lift the load
Increases the effort needed to lift the load
questions.explain: More supporting rope sections share the load, so less effort is needed to lift it, though the rope must be pulled further.

questions.q: Motion that moves back and forth in a straight line is called:
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion is repeated back-and-forth movement in a straight line, as seen in a piston or a sewing-machine needle.

questions.q: For a simple gear train, the gear ratio is calculated as:
options: Driver teeth multiplied by driven teeth
Driven teeth added to driver teeth
Driver teeth divided by driven teeth
Driven teeth divided by driver teeth
questions.explain: Gear ratio equals the number of teeth on the driven gear divided by the number on the driver gear.

questions.q: A first-class lever, such as a seesaw, has the fulcrum positioned:
options: Only at the very end of the load
Between the effort and the load
Beyond both the effort and load
At the same point as the load
questions.explain: In a first-class lever the fulcrum (pivot) sits between the effort and the load, as on a seesaw or pair of scissors.

questions.q: Motion that swings back and forth on a pivot, like a pendulum, is called:
questions.explain: Oscillating motion swings back and forth around a fixed pivot point, as a pendulum does.

questions.q: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?
questions.explain: In a wheelbarrow the load sits between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort (handles), making it a second-class lever.

questions.q: A driver pulley of 100 mm diameter drives a 50 mm pulley. The smaller pulley will turn:
options: At the same speed as the driver
questions.explain: A smaller driven pulley rotates faster than a larger driver pulley, increasing output speed.

questions.q: In a gear train, an idler gear is added mainly to:
options: Reverse the direction of the output gear without changing the ratio
Change the overall gear ratio of the train
questions.explain: An idler gear sits between driver and driven gears to reverse the output's direction; it does not affect the overall gear ratio.

questions.q: A linkage in a mechanism is used to:
options: Change the direction or type of motion between parts
questions.explain: Linkages are bars connected by pivots that transfer or change the direction and nature of motion in a mechanism.

questions.q: A crank and slider mechanism converts:
options: Reciprocating motion into oscillating motion only
questions.explain: A crank and slider turns rotary motion into reciprocating (back-and-forth) linear motion, as in an engine.

questions.q: A driver gear has 10 teeth and the driven gear has 30 teeth. The gear ratio is:
questions.explain: Gear ratio = driven 30 divided by driver 10 = 3, written 3:1, meaning the driver turns three times for each turn of the driven gear.

questions.q: In a third-class lever, such as tweezers, the effort is positioned:
options: Between the fulcrum and the load
questions.explain: A third-class lever has the effort applied between the fulcrum and the load, as with tweezers or a fishing rod.

questions.q: A rack and pinion mechanism converts:
options: Linear motion into oscillating motion only
questions.explain: A rotating pinion gear meshes with a straight toothed rack to convert rotary motion into linear motion.

questions.q: A force that pulls or stretches a material is called:
questions.explain: Tension is a pulling or stretching force, while compression is a squashing force.

questions.q: A bevel gear is mainly used to:
options: Transmit rotary motion through an angle, often 90 degrees
questions.explain: Bevel gears mesh at an angle, commonly 90 degrees, to change the direction of rotary drive.

questions.q: A worm gear driving a worm wheel is often used because it:
options: Gives a large speed reduction and high torque in a compact space
questions.explain: A worm and wheel produces a large gear reduction, lowering speed and increasing torque in a small space.

questions.q: Mechanical advantage is gained when a mechanism allows:
options: Energy to be created from nothing
A larger effort to move a smaller load
A small effort to move a larger load
No load to be moved at all
questions.explain: Mechanical advantage means a machine lets a small input effort overcome a larger output load.

questions.q: A force that squashes or pushes a material together is called:
questions.explain: Compression is a squashing force that pushes material together; tension by contrast pulls it apart.

questions.q: A cam and follower mechanism is used to convert:
questions.explain: As a cam rotates, its profile pushes the follower up and down, converting rotary motion into reciprocating motion.

questions.q: Rotary motion is best described as movement that is:
options: Back and forth in a straight line
Turning in a circle around a central point
Swinging back and forth on a pivot
In a straight line in one direction
questions.explain: Rotary motion is movement in a circle around a central axis, such as a wheel or gear turning.
